$why_source: The canonical copy lives at the path above. Every other language VENDORS this file byte for byte and is found by this field rather than by a list somebody maintains (estate-gates C14).
comment: Cross-language vectors for an agent's own access token (RFC 9068, typ at+jwt, DPoP-bound by RFC 9449), as vouchryx's client_credentials grant mints it. Every verifier (Go: this repository's delegation.VerifyAccess, VerifyRelayedAccess and Verify; Rust: tokenfuse's crates/delegation verify_agent_token, verify_relayed_agent_token and verify_delegation) MUST answer each case as stated. A case is fixed bytes: `jws` is the token, `dpop` the proof (absent means no proof), `now` the verifier's clock in Unix seconds. `verifier` is `agent` (the token and its proof, with a fresh replay cache), `relayed` (the token alone, no proof) or `delegation` (the delegation-chain verifier, which must refuse typ at+jwt). `method`, `url` and `audience` override `config` when present, and an `audience` of "" is a door with none configured. `revoke` is the revocation hook: it answers true for a call naming its `jti` or its `subject`, and false for anything else or when absent. `expect` is `accept` or the refusal, named in tokenfuse's Refusal vocabulary snake_cased; `verified` is what an accepted agent token yields. A `known_divergence` records, from source reading, a verifier that does not yet answer as stated. `replay` holds sequences for the proof replay cache: one cache of `cap` per sequence, each step a jti recorded at `now`. The keys under `test_only_keys` exist for this table alone and sign nothing else.

outcomes.audience: aud does not name the configured audience, or none is configured.
outcomes.bad_signature: No key in the set verifies it: an unknown kid, another key's signature, or an algorithm the key type does not permit.
outcomes.issuer: iss is not exactly the configured issuer.
outcomes.malformed: Not this kind of token: wrong or absent typ, no kid, or claims an agent token never carries or always carries.
outcomes.no_proof: A bound token presented with no proof.
outcomes.revoked: The revocation hook named the token's jti or its agent.
outcomes.wrong_key: The proof fails, is by another key, or does not name this token in ath.

replay_outcomes.full: The current generation is at its cap; nothing is forgotten to make room.

not_in_this_table: Shapes both verifiers refuse under different internal names, so a case would test a library's error mapping rather than a rule:
a header with alg none or no alg (Rust: malformed, its header parser knows no such algorithm; Go: bad_signature);
a token with no iss or no exp, or a claim of the wrong JSON type (Rust: bad_signature, from deserialization; Go: issuer, expired or the rule the claim feeds);
a JSON member repeated (Rust refuses it in deserialization; Go keeps the last) and dates written as fractions.
All of these are signed bytes only the issuer can produce.

cases.name: a good agent token verifies with its holder's proof
cases.why: The shape vouchryx mints. If this refuses, every agent is locked out.

cases.name: the second key of a rotating set verifies by its own kid
cases.why: A key set holds two keys during a rotation; the kid names the one that signed.

cases.name: an audience array that names this resource is accepted
cases.why: RFC 9068 allows aud to be an array; one naming this resource is for it.

cases.name: twenty-nine seconds past exp is inside the leeway
cases.why: Two hosts' clocks drift; a refusal in the second a token turns over is an outage.

cases.name: an iat exactly the leeway ahead is accepted
cases.why: The leeway applies to a fast issuer clock as well as a slow door.

cases.name: a query string on the request is not a different request
cases.why: htu is the request URI without its query (RFC 9449 4.3).

cases.name: a revocation naming another agent does not refuse this one
cases.why: The negative control for the revocation cases: a hook that refused everything would pass them.

cases.name: typ JWT is not an agent token
cases.why: typ decides, both ways: a delegation token or an ID-JAG is never an agent token.

cases.name: a token with no typ is not an agent token
cases.why: An absent typ is not at+jwt.

cases.name: the long media type application/at+jwt is not accepted
cases.why: Both verifiers compare the short form exactly, which is what vouchryx mints. RFC 9068 2.1 also allows the long form; accepting it is a decision for both languages at once.

cases.name: an agent token is not a delegation
cases.why: The delegation verifier refuses typ at+jwt, so an agent token is never read as a chain of one.

cases.name: an at+jwt token carrying a chain is not a delegation
cases.why: The shape the typ rule exists for: a delegation's claims under the agent token's typ.

cases.name: a delegation typed JWT still verifies as a delegation
cases.why: The control for the two cases above: the typ rule refuses one typ, not every delegation.

cases.name: a token with no kid is malformed
cases.why: No kid, no key: there is nothing to match, and trying every key would make one compromised key a skeleton key.

cases.name: a kid no key in the set has is refused
cases.why: The kid names one key; a kid naming none verifies nothing.

cases.name: a token signed by a key other than the one its kid names is refused
cases.why: The second key of the set signs, the token names the first.

cases.name: a token signed by a key outside the set is refused
cases.why: A stranger's key under the issuer's kid.

cases.name: HS256 with the issuer's public key as the secret is refused
cases.why: The classic algorithm confusion: the algorithm comes from the key type, never from the header.

cases.name: ES384 over a P-256 key is refused
cases.why: An algorithm name means one curve; a P-256 key does not verify under ES384.

cases.name: a token from another issuer is refused
cases.why: iss is exact.

cases.name: an issuer with a trailing slash is refused
cases.why: Exact means exact: no normalisation of iss.

cases.name: an issuer written as an array is refused
cases.why: iss is one string. RFC 7519 4.1.1 defines it as a single StringOrURI.

known_divergence.why: jsonwebtoken 10.4.0 validation.rs:317-329 accepts an issuer array that intersects the configured issuer; tokenfuse passes its validation through decode_claims.

cases.name: a token for another resource is refused
cases.why: aud is required and exact.

cases.name: a token for a prefix of this resource is refused
cases.why: A prefix match is how a service ends up trusting a neighbour.

cases.name: a token for this resource with more after it is refused
cases.why: The other direction of a prefix match.

cases.name: an audience array that does not name this resource is refused
cases.why: An array is accepted only when it names this resource.

cases.name: a token with no audience is refused
cases.why: Required means present: a token minted for no resource is not minted for this one.

known_divergence.why: jsonwebtoken 10.4.0 validation.rs:334-357 checks aud only when the claim is present unless "aud" is a required spec claim, and decode_claims requires only exp and iss.

cases.name: a door with no audience configured refuses a good token
cases.why: An empty configured audience refuses everything rather than accepting any resource.

cases.name: a door with no audience configured refuses a token for the empty audience
cases.why: The one token an empty configured audience could be read to match is still refused.

cases.name: thirty seconds past exp is expired
cases.why: The leeway's edge: now >= exp + 30 refuses.

cases.name: an iat thirty-one seconds ahead is not yet valid
cases.why: Past the leeway a token from the future is refused.

cases.name: a sub that is a user is malformed
cases.why: An agent token names an agent.

cases.name: a sub that names no agent after the scheme is malformed
cases.why: agent:// alone names nobody.

cases.name: a client_id that is another agent is malformed
cases.why: RFC 9068 2.2: the agent is the client, so the two are one string.

cases.name: a token with no client_id is malformed
cases.why: client_id is required by RFC 9068 2.2.

cases.name: a token with no jti is malformed
cases.why: jti is what revocation names a token by.

cases.name: a token with an act claim is malformed
cases.why: An agent token acts for nobody; a chain belongs to a delegation token.

cases.name: a token with no cnf is not bound
cases.why: vouchryx binds everything it mints; an unbound token is from somewhere else.

cases.name: a token with an empty cnf.jkt is not bound
cases.why: An empty thumbprint binds to nothing.

cases.name: a bound token with no proof is refused
cases.why: A sender-constrained token is never checked as a bearer token.

cases.name: a stranger's proof is the wrong key
cases.why: The bytes of a stolen token are not enough.

cases.name: a proof with no ath is the wrong key
cases.why: RFC 9449 4.2: a proof beside an access token names it.

cases.name: a proof naming another token of the same holder is the wrong key
cases.why: Without ath a proof binds a request to a key, not to a token.

cases.name: a proof for another URL is the wrong key
cases.why: A proof is for one request.

cases.name: a proof for another method is the wrong key
cases.why: A proof is for one request.

cases.name: a proof sixty-one seconds old is the wrong key
cases.why: A proof is for one moment, within sixty seconds either way.

cases.name: a proof whose jti is longer than 256 bytes is the wrong key
cases.why: A client chooses its jti and the replay cache stores it.

cases.name: a proof with no jti is the wrong key
cases.why: Without a jti nothing can make a proof single use.

cases.name: a proof whose method is written in lower case is the wrong key
cases.why: RFC 9110 methods are case sensitive (agent-stack-go invariant 24).

known_divergence.why: crates/dpop/src/lib.rs verify_proof compares htm with eq_ignore_ascii_case.

cases.name: a proof whose host is written in upper case is the same request
cases.why: RFC 9449 4.3 applies RFC 3986 6.2.2.1: scheme and host compare without case (agent-stack-go invariant 24).

known_divergence.why: crates/dpop/src/lib.rs verify_proof compares htu and the URL as strings, query trimmed, with no case fold of scheme or host.

cases.name: a token whose agent is revoked is refused
cases.why: Stopping one agent is one revocation naming it.

cases.name: a token whose jti is revoked is refused
cases.why: A revocation may name one token.

cases.name: a revocation does not mask a stolen proof
cases.why: The hook is asked last, so a token failing its proof is refused for the proof.

cases.name: a relayed token verifies without a proof
cases.why: Another door of this deployment checked the proof; everything else is checked again.

cases.name: a relayed token with no cnf is not bound
cases.why: Relayed skips the proof, never the binding.

cases.name: a relayed token past its leeway is expired
cases.why: Relayed skips the proof, never the clock.

cases.name: a relayed token typed JWT is malformed
cases.why: Relayed skips the proof, never the typ.

cases.name: a relayed revoked token is refused
cases.why: Relayed skips the proof, never the revocation list.

cases.name: a relayed token at a door with no audience is refused
cases.why: Relayed skips the proof, never the audience.

replay.name: a second use of one jti is refused
replay.why: A proof is single use inside its window.

replay.name: distinct jtis are all admitted
replay.why: The negative control: a cache that refused everything would pass the case above.

replay.name: a jti survives every moment a proof carrying it could still be fresh
replay.why: A proof's iat may sit a window ahead of now and now a window past iat, so a generation is two windows.

replay.name: a jti recorded in the last second of a generation outlives the next one
replay.why: The rotation boundary: the previous generation is consulted for a whole generation more.

replay.name: a full cache refuses rather than forgetting
replay.why: Forgetting under pressure is a replay guard that stops guarding exactly when somebody pushes on it.

replay.name: a clock that walks backwards does not empty the cache
replay.why: A start time that only moves forward: stepping a clock back never rotates the generations.
